Aisha to publish the Aug outage postmortem + mitigation plan (by 2025-10-20)
Maya to circulate Private deployment checklist & SOC2 evidence request (by 2025-10-21)

summary: Company all-hands covering Q3 results, customer trends, reliability updates, product roadmap highlights (Optimize, Dedicated enhancements, Private), hiring update, and a short Q&A. Leadership emphasized production reliability, enterprise readiness for Private deployments, and balanced growth across hosted and Dedicated offerings.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park: Good morning, everybody. Welcome to the October all-hands. Thanks for joining, we packed a lot in today - Q3 review, reliability updates, product roadmap, and a few folks from sales and engineering will jump in. Uh, quick housekeeping, recording is on.

[00:28] Jordan Park: Quick note, if you have questions drop them in Q&A or raise your hand in the chat. We'll try to get to as many as we can. First slide, Q3 highlights - revenue beat plan, usage up 42% quarter-over-quarter, and Dedicated bookings increased for enterprise accounts.

[01:05] Aisha Rahman: On reliability, we had that August incident - we own that, we learned a lot. Postmortem is nearly finished, we'll publish next week. The root cause was a combination of autoscaler race conditions and a kernel edge-case with a quantized model fallback path. There were also some observability gaps that made diagnosis slower.

[01:40] Jordan Park: Thanks Aisha. Important to call out the customer impact - some Dedicated customers saw higher latencies for a few minutes, and a handful of hosted customers experienced throttling. We had fallbacks but we need stronger prevention.

[02:05] Maya Chen: To add, we've shipped a safety patch to the runtime that reduces the race window and improved our kernel selection logic. We also added more golden signals to the console dashboards. The fix's initial rollout looks stable in staging and to early Dedicated clusters.

[02:42] Audience (chat): When will we have the changelog / docs?

[02:50] Aisha Rahman: Changelog and a short remediation guide will be in the engineering channel and we'll push to the public docs later this week.

[03:12] Liam O'Connor: On product roadmap - three themes for Q4: reliability hardening, Optimize feature rollout (batching suggestions, quantization profiles), and Private onboarding improvements (VPC templates, KMS integrations). We'll demo a preview of Optimize in a few minutes.

[03:45] Ethan Ruiz: Sales highlight - enterprise funnel remains strong. We're seeing procurement timelines lengthen with some accounts asking for on-prem/private options plus SOC 2 evidence. Pricing pressure is real - many prospects ask about latency vs cost tradeoffs, and they frequently mention Anthropic and OpenAI as reference points.

[04:22] Jordan Park: On competition - good to be aware, but our thesis remains serving and economics: predictable latency and cost controls. Emphasis on the developer experience too.

[04:45] Jordan Park: Quick hiring update - we are prioritizing SRE, infra, and security hires. People Ops will share a pipeline update. Also launching a small IC recognition program.

[05:10] Priya Nair: Recruiting note - we have 18 open roles in infra & product. Please refer candidates, bonus for referrals.

[05:32] Liam O'Connor: Demo time - quick tour of Redwood Optimize alpha. It suggests batch sizes based on request histograms, recommends quantization profile per model, and surfaces expected cost/latency delta.

[06:05] (demo noises, screen share)

[06:25] Liam O'Connor: Example: for a customer with bursty traffic we recommend prefix caching plus small-batch mode; estimated cost savings 20% without noticeable latency change. This is early but promising.

[06:58] Audience Q: Will Optimize change runtime defaults?

[07:05] Maya Chen: No, defaults remain safe. Optimize gives suggested config and a simulation; operators can approve rollouts. We'll add automatic canaries down the road.

[07:30] Jordan Park: Security update - SOC 2 readiness ongoing. Maya, quick status?

[07:38] Maya Chen: We're on track for scope completion; a few control gaps around vendor onboarding and audit log retention lengths - we'll address both with policy and console changes. We expect to engage an auditor for readiness review by end of Q4.

[08:05] Audience (raised hand): Any update on Private / on-prem packages?

[08:12] Aisha Rahman: Yes - Private now supports customer-managed KMS (early access) and we have a VPC deployment template that reduces setup time. The on-prem package is still in alpha; we want a couple of pilot customers before GA.

[08:40] Ethan Ruiz: From sales feedback, customers want clear SLAs and an audit bundle. We're working on a Private offering package that includes a compliance add-on and extended support levels.

[09:05] Jordan Park: OK, Q&A rapid fire.

[09:10] Audience: Will we change pricing if Optimize reduces costs?

[09:15] Jordan Park: Pricing conversations ongoing - goal is to pass value to customers while sustaining growth. We may pilot volume discounts tied to usage patterns and Optimize adoption.

[09:34] Audience (chat): Any update on EU data residency?

[09:40] Maya Chen: We're expanding regions and working with partners. EU data residency is a priority for some customers; we'll provide a regional routing policy soon.

[10:05] Aisha Rahman: Quick reliability note - we now have auto-fallback to compatible model variants when a kernel error occurs, that reduces customer visible errors. Still more work on tracing and KV cache consistency.

[10:40] Jordan Park: Before we wrap, hiring - we want to move faster on SRE and product ops. People Ops will circulate interview templates to reduce cycle time.

[11:05] Priya Nair: We'll also publish interview rubrics and schedule open office hours for interviewers.

[11:30] Jordan Park: Closing remarks - thank you. We grew a lot this year but the work is to make the service predictable and enterprise ready. The leadership team is focused on reliability, Private product-market fit, and shipping Optimize. We'll follow up with the docs and action items.

[11:58] Jordan Park: Recap of next steps in chat and I'll send the OKR deck after the meeting. Thanks all.

[12:20] End recording.
